# Results — Study 645 (ECB Announcement Effect)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **euro-area
equities drift or react systematically around ECB Governing Council monetary-policy decision
days** — tested on the full hardcoded calendar of **208 scheduled ECB decisions 2005-2026**
against FEZ (the SPDR EURO STOXX 50 ETF) and EURUSD=X. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month). Fingerprints `d1fc0178e274` (FEZ) / `c85271b5a68f` (EURUSD=X).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily FEZ raw OHLC (5,406 rows) + EURUSD=X OHLC (5,574 rows), 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30 |
| ECB calendar | **hardcoded** table of **208 scheduled** Governing Council monetary-policy decision dates 2005-01-13 → 2026-06-11 (ECB year-ahead schedule press releases 2005-2014 monthly era; ECB monetary-policy-statement archive 2015-2026 six-week era; rate-change dates cross-checked against FRED `ECBDFR`) |
| Events | **207** of 208 decision days sit on the FEZ tape; **5,198** other trading days |
| Data quirk (named) | the scheduled **2013-07-04** decision fell on US Independence Day — FEZ (NYSEArca-listed) did not trade, so that meeting drops from the FEZ-side statistics (kept in the ECB calendar itself) |
| Statistics | Welch *t* for the group splits (non-overlapping single-day events); **Newey-West (5 lags)** *t* on the decision-day dummy regression as the serial-correlation-robust cross-check (load-bearing for the realized-range test, which is autocorrelated); a two-sided 20-seed × 1,000-draw random-calendar placebo; Wilson interval on the hit rate |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention (third axis only): FEZ entered at the **prior session's close** — the calendar is public months ahead, zero look-ahead — and exited at the decision-day close; one round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV; long-only, no borrow |

No survivorship on the Signal axis: FEZ and EURUSD=X are baskets/rates, not a hand-picked
survivor panel.

## The headline — decision-day FEZ return vs all other days

| quantity | decision days | all other days |
|---|--:|--:|
| mean FEZ log return | −0.103% | +0.015% |
| gap | **−0.118 pts** | |
| Welch *t* | **−0.82** | |
| Newey-West *t* (dummy regression, 5 lags) | **−0.83** | |
| hit rate (FEZ up) | 114/207 = 55.1% (Wilson 95% [48.3%, 61.7%]) | |
| random-calendar placebo (two-sided, 20,000 draws) | observed −0.1031% vs placebo mean +0.0141% (sd 0.1093%) → **p = 0.345** | |

The directional claim is flatly **not there**. The average decision day moves FEZ by a tenth of
a point *against* the folklore's implicit direction, the gap is well inside noise on both the
raw split and the HAC cross-check, and a random 207-day calendar matches or beats it about a
third of the time. No drift, no directional reaction — not even a faint one.

## The realized-range cross-check — decision days ARE louder

| quantity | decision days | other days | ratio | Welch *t* | NW(5) *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| FEZ (H−L)/prev close | **1.492%** | 1.257% | **1.19×** | **+2.66** | **+2.83** | **0.0008** |

Unlike the drift, the **volatility** side of the claim clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar three
separate ways — raw Welch, the autocorrelation-robust Newey-West cross-check (range is strongly
serially correlated, so this is the load-bearing check, not a formality), and a two-sided
20,000-draw placebo. Decision days run genuinely louder — about **1.19×** a normal session —
even though price direction on those same days is a coin flip.

**Caveat, said out loud:** the full-sample effect is decisive, but split by era (below) *neither
half alone* clears *t* = 2 — the full-sample power comes from pooling 207 events, not from a
robust effect visible in either sub-period on its own.

## EURUSD reaction — the FX leg doesn't react more either

| quantity | decision days | other days | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| EURUSD \|log return\| | 0.455% | 0.436% | **+0.65** |

If the announcement were moving markets hard, the currency leg — which prices the same policy
surprise directly — would be the first place to look. It isn't: EURUSD's absolute daily move on
decision days is statistically indistinguishable from any other day.

## Event window — a Lucca-Moench-style pre-meeting drift analog (FEZ return %, Welch *t* vs far days)

| offset | −5 | −4 | −3 | −2 | −1 | **0** | +1 | +2 | +3 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| mean % | +0.105 | −0.099 | −0.203 | +0.171 | +0.146 | **−0.103** | +0.017 | −0.112 | +0.032 |
| Welch *t* | +0.85 | −1.10 | −1.58 | +1.23 | +1.11 | **−0.84** | −0.01 | −0.91 | +0.12 |

- **Pre-meeting run-up:** cumulative [−5..−1] is **+0.121%/meeting** at one-sample
  *t* = **+0.54** — no analog of the Fed's pre-FOMC drift shows up here; every single offset in
  the nine-day window sits below *t* = 1.6 in absolute value.
- **Persistence:** day 0 isn't even the largest bar in the window (day −3 is bigger in
  magnitude) — there's no clean "the event happens, then it's over" signature the way the FOMC
  vol crush shows one.

## Era contrast — monthly era vs the 6-week-cycle era (split 2015-01-01, justified: the Governing Council's own structural change)

| era | ECB-day FEZ return | n | within-era Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2005 → 2014 (monthly) | −0.137% | 115 | −0.66 |
| 2015 → 2026 (6-week) | −0.061% | 92 | −0.46 |
| Welch *t* of the difference (late − early) | | | +0.27 |

| era | ECB-day FEZ range | n | within-era Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2005 → 2014 (monthly) | 1.722% | 115 | +1.70 |
| 2015 → 2026 (6-week) | 1.206% | 92 | +1.65 |
| Welch *t* of the difference (late − early) | | | **−3.18** |

Neither the (already-absent) drift nor its non-existence changed across the cadence switch
(diff *t* = +0.27). The range level itself has genuinely fallen (diff *t* = −3.18) — mostly the
2008-2012 crisis years sitting in the "monthly" bucket inflate that era's baseline volatility,
not a change in the *ECB-specific* bump, whose within-era Welch *t*'s (1.70 and 1.65) are
themselves statistically twins.

## Third axis — "costs on a timer": hold FEZ for the decision day only

Enter the prior close (calendar public months ahead — zero look-ahead), exit the decision-day
close; 207 scheduled decisions on the FEZ tape.

| one-way cost | gross | net | ~%/yr at 8 events |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | −10.3 bps/event | **−20.3 bps/event** | −1.62% |
| 10 bps | −10.3 bps/event | −30.3 bps/event | −2.42% |
| 20 bps | −10.3 bps/event | −50.3 bps/event | −4.02% |

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| ECB-day FEZ vs other-day FEZ | −10.3 bps vs +1.5 bps (Welch *t* = **−0.82**) |
| hit rate | 55.1% |
| worst single decision day | **−13.3%** |

There is nothing to harvest here even before costs: the gross average is *negative*, so every
cost basis point charged just makes an already-losing rule worse. A trader "riding the ECB day"
would have been long a coin flip with a fat left tail (−13.3% on the worst day) for a negative
expected return.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic i.i.d.-return world with scheduled pseudo-decision days every 22nd business day
(≈ the 6-week cadence) and a TUNABLE planted decision-day drift; no network.

| world | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (drift = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.07** (sd 0.73), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted drift = +0.5% (seed 645) | **+7.48** |

The detector never fires on the null and lights up cleanly on a planted effect. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED** (*Real on the vol · None on the drift*). Decision-day FEZ returns show no
  directional edge (Welch *t* = **−0.82**, NW *t* = **−0.83**, placebo *p* = 0.345) and EURUSD's
  absolute move doesn't differ from a normal day either (*t* = +0.65) — but the FEZ realized
  range genuinely runs **1.19×** louder on decision days, clearing *t* ≥ 2 three separate ways
  (Welch +2.66, NW +2.83, placebo *p* = 0.0008). Caveat named: neither era split alone clears
  *t* = 2 on the range bump (1.70 / 1.65) — the full-sample significance leans on pooling all
  207 events.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The only rule with a pulse (hold FEZ for the decision day) loses
  money **gross**, before a single basis point of cost, with a −13.3% worst day. There is no
  drift to harvest and the vol elevation itself isn't a directional edge — it is exactly where
  options are already marked up going into a scheduled event.
- **"Louder, not directional"? — CONFIRMED.** Decision days are measurably noisier
  (range 1.19×, *t* ≥ 2.66 two ways, placebo *p* < 0.001) while price direction on those same
  days (FEZ, *t* = −0.82) and the FX reaction (EURUSD, *t* = +0.65) are both statistically
  indistinguishable from any other Thursday. The market resolves uncertainty on ECB day; it
  just doesn't resolve it in a predictable direction.
